summary: Round 4: the geometry is identical to rounds 2-3 (same part volumes, walls and requirement values), so the engineering stands. Each joint has a hard stop at about -2 deg, flexion runs clear to 80/80/70, the pivots are ground-shoulder screws, and both FEA cases pass (4.6 and 10.5 MPa vs 24). The generated ASSEMBLY.md now has the real tools, an insert step per part (flush-to-low, plate, trim the lip), gentle shoulder-screw torque with a free-turn check, and the tendon/crimp-sleeve step. bom.md carries the McMaster order number and 'tighten gently'. Only minor items remain.

findings.issue: Order and practicality of the tendon step. The note is nested under 'Fit distal' and says 'After the dip pivot screw below', so it reads before the screw it depends on. Threading a braid ~90 mm from the base's back face through 2.2 mm channels that hand over into the 0.3 mm lap gap and knuckle grooves at three joints, after everything is assembled, will snag at each channel/groove transition unless the tip is stiffened.
findings.fix: Make tendons their own final step after the dip pivot, rather than a sub-bullet. Add: stiffen the line end with a drop of CA (or use a fine wire leader) and feed it with the finger slightly curled, then check it slides with no snag before fitting the crimp sleeve. Add a crimping tool or pliers to the tools list.

findings.issue: Side play is unchanged and documented: 0.45 mm axial and ~1.7 deg tilt per joint, a few mm of fingertip wobble.
findings.fix: Accept as documented, or use the 4.2 mm free hole / 0.2 mm PTFE washer from DESIGN s2 after the test pair.

findings.issue: Cosmetic cusp where the pocket circle cuts the child's top-band lug. It is documented and not loaded.
findings.fix: Optional: start the lug at z = RH in the top band.

findings.issue: The wall check still reports 1.12 mm (p2), below the 1.2 mm reliable minimum, at the knot pockets / grooves.
findings.fix: Move the pockets or channel 0.1-0.2 mm.

findings.issue: Knuckle-face grooves are built from 10-deg steps (serrated fan). A taut 0.5 mm line clears the ridges; a slack or 0.8 mm line may drag on them.
findings.fix: Acceptable. Use one swept groove if the line frays in testing.
